title: Directional billing + streaming credit rollover pilot for Hosted API
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
Run a targeted pilot to evaluate a combined mechanism: per-direction token rates (separate input/ingress vs output/egress multipliers) plus a controlled rollover of unused committed credits into streaming credits at a conversion ratio. The goal is to measure behavioral changes, revenue sensitivity, and operational surface area for enterprise contracts that want predictable spend while supporting bursty streaming workloads.

Hypothesis:
1) Separating input vs output pricing with a small output premium (e.g., output_rate=1.15*input_rate) more fairly captures compute + memory cost for generative workloads and reduces cross-subsidization from embedding-heavy ingestion.
2) Allowing a bounded rollover of unused committed ingress credits into streaming/egress credits (convert at 30% value, monthly cap) will increase adoption of committed tiers by teams with bursty output, while limiting revenue erosion.
3) A handshake-based streaming grace (first 5 seconds of a stream are billed at reduced per-token rate when under a rollover-backed credit) will reduce SLA-triggered fallbacks and improve developer experience for real-time apps.

Experiment arms:
A: Baseline (control) - current asymmetric IO pricing with no rollover.
B: Directional only - separate input/output rates, no rollover. Proposed rates: input_rate = $0.000012 / input-token, output_rate = $0.000014 / output-token.
C: Directional + Rollover - same rates as B and allow rollover of unused ingress committed credits into output credits at 30% conversion, monthly cap = 10% of committed volume.
D: Directional + Rollover + Stream Grace - same as C plus a streaming handshake grace: first 5s of steady streaming for qualifying routes billed at 75% of output_rate when consumed against rollover credits.

Metrics to collect (primary/secondary):
- Revenue per active customer (primary)
- Net new committed capacity signups (primary)
- Effective blended rate (revenue / total tokens) by direction (secondary)
- Burst coverage rate: fraction of streaming bursts that consume from rollover credits vs fallback (secondary)
- Churn and downgrades for customers > $10k/mo (secondary)
- Operational errors or disputes logged per 10k billing events (secondary)

Acceptance criteria for progression:
- Revenue delta for arm C >= -2% vs baseline while committed capacity signups increase by >= 8% in pilot cohort OR
- Arm D reduces streaming fallbacks by >= 30% compared to baseline without >5% revenue downside compared to baseline.

Telemetry & implementation notes for Eng:
- New billing fields: billed_input_tokens, billed_output_tokens, consumed_rollover_credits, rollover_conversion_rate, is_streaming_grace_applied (all reported in per-request billing events).
- Add sampling for token-level traces for first 100M tokens in pilot to validate rate application.
- Expose dashboards: per-account effective rate, rollover balance usage heatmap, streaming grace utilization. Suggested dashboard links: https://datadog.redwood.ai/dash/hosted-pricing/pilot-91245, https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-pricing/pilot-91245.

Billing formula (prototype):
- billed_input = input_tokens * input_rate
- billed_output = output_tokens * output_rate
- rollover_credit_value = unused_committed_input_tokens * input_rate * rollover_conversion_rate (e.g., 0.30)
- rollover_applied_to_output reduces billed_output up to rollover_credit_value for the billing period
- streaming_handshake_discount applies only when is_streaming_grace_applied == true and rollover_credit covers the stream; discount = 25% off output_rate for first 5s of stream.

Legal / Contract / SQ alignment:
- Work with Enterprise Sales and Legal to surface rollover conversion and cap language in term sheets and security questionnaire answers. Questions to pre-answer for SOC/ISO customer SQs: how are credits accounted, auditable ledger for rollover conversions, and dispute resolution windows. Draft SQ language: "Committed credits are applied first to ingress usage. A capped portion of unused ingress credits may be converted to egress credits at a predefined conversion rate; all conversions are recorded in the customer's billing ledger and available for audit for 12 months."

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-2: Finalize rate and conversion parameters with Finance and Legal. Implement telemetry and billing-event schema (ENG).
- Week 3-4: Internal dogfood with 5 internal teams and 3 early enterprise customers (opt-in). Collect initial telemetry.
- Week 5-8: Run pilot on 50 customers across different workload profiles (embedding-heavy, chat-heavy, retrieval-augmented streams).
- Week 9: Evaluate against acceptance criteria and recommend full productization, adjustments, or cancel.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Rollover creates arbitrage that erodes revenue. Mitigation: strict cap (10%) and low conversion rate (30%), monitor in real time and enable immediate rate adjustments.
- Risk: Complexity creates billing disputes. Mitigation: full ledger export and transparency UI for pilot customers; one-click dispute flow and 30-day resolution SLA.
- Risk: Implementation burden on runtime telemetry. Mitigation: begin with sampled telemetry and bill reconciliation job rather than per-request billing in first month.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Either C meets revenue / signup thresholds (revenue delta >= -2% and committed signups +8%), or D meets streaming fallback reduction target (>=30%) with revenue downside <= 5%. 2) Billing events and dashboards implemented and validated. 3) Legal and Sales approve contract language & SQ wording.
plan_steps: 1) Align final rates and conversion caps with Finance/Legal. 2) Define billing-event schema and add sampling plan. 3) Build dashboard and ledger export. 4) Implement pilot flag and opt-in UI for enterprise accounts. 5) Execute dogfood and enterprise opt-in cohort. 6) Analyze and decide (productize/iterate/stop).
